current_executor_getter.return: x0 raw executor pointer or null

setter_evidence_only.warning: Uses the special TLV bootstrap convention; x8 is not generally AAPCS64 callee-saved. Never set TLS to impersonate an executor.

getter_consumer.behavior: Null check, then dynamic_cast from RTTI 0x9fb1808 to 0x9fb1a78.

research_component.construct: Reject missing getter/expected pointer, then reject null or mismatched current executor before NativeBody/factory.
research_component.control: Check current executor on every cancel/expire, then retain ResearchOperation factory-thread lifecycle token check before state mutation/request cancel.
research_component.observation: snapshot and task_id do not query TLS; callbacks can arrive on other threads.
research_component.destruction: No implicit TLS query or native cancellation.
research_component.supplied_by_caller: Proven expected executor raw base, service/options/module lifetime, function pointers and complete scheduler/cleanup contract.

limitations: Checks are entry guards, not an atomic lifetime or shutdown lease.
Pointer equality and a factory-thread token do not prove coroutine identity, core state, runtime readiness or that the expected pointer is live.
The worker proof covers the selected normal path, not exceptions or every shutdown path.
Group cancellation can still act outside these request-control guards; state-zero reachability and final argument cleanup remain unresolved.
No TLS setter, scheduler, loader, native address resolver, retry, attachment or product integration is provided.
Owned callback/response success never establishes independent delivery.
